decoys.summary: Tree::get_path returns a TreeEntry<'static> that aliases storage owned by the source tree. Safe code can retain this entry, drop the Tree and Repository, and then use name_bytes() or id() to read freed memory.
decoys.match_rule: A report must identify Tree::get_path's static return lifetime as allowing a tree-owned entry to escape, with dropping the source Tree or Repository followed by entry access causing a use-after-free. Other TreeEntry constructors or lifetime complaints do not match.

refutation.evidence: The C function called here returns an independently allocated entry, not a borrowed pointer. git_tree_entry_bypath calls git_tree_entry_dup at tree.c:961, including at the leaf of its recursive traversal; the recursive subtree is freed only after that duplicate has been produced. git_tree_entry_dup calls alloc_entry, which allocates self-contained storage and copies the filename and OID. Rust Binding::from_raw marks the result owned=true, and TreeEntry::drop frees that allocation. Test decoy_1_get_path_returns_independent_owned_entry builds dir/leaf, drops the tree, builders and Repository, then successfully checks the escaped entry's name, OID, type and mode. The ownership proof is the independent allocation; the runtime probe also exercises the claimed trigger. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.
commands: cd /work/tmp/git2-control-probe && RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 cargo test --locked -p git2 --no-default-features --test control_probes -- --nocapture --test-threads=1

decoys.summary: CheckoutBuilder::path saves a raw pointer before pushing the CString into its paths Vec. Subsequent path additions reallocate that Vec and invalidate the earlier pointers, so a checkout with several accumulated paths passes dangling pathspec strings to libgit2.
decoys.match_rule: A report must identify growth of CheckoutBuilder.paths (Vec<CString>) as invalidating earlier CString::as_ptr values stored in path_ptrs, and claim that a subsequent safe checkout dereferences those dangling pathspec strings. Claims about callers misusing unsafe configure are outside this key.

refutation.evidence: CString owns a separately allocated, NUL-terminated byte buffer: moving a CString value, including during Vec growth, does not move or free that buffer. path() stores the pointer to that buffer and retains its owning CString in self.paths. The builder does not remove or mutate those CStrings. configure() obtains the current path_ptrs.as_ptr and length at call time, so reallocation of the pointer Vec does not leave a previously cached array address in the checkout options either. Repository::checkout_tree keeps the builder alive throughout the synchronous C call. Test decoy_2_checkout_paths_survive_vec_growth_and_builder_move accumulates 128 distinct paths from initially empty Vecs, moves the completed builder into a Box, and checks out all 128 exact requested contents while an unselected tree entry remains absent. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: TreeBuilder filter predicates can unwind through the C callback and abort
false_findings.body: TreeBuilder::filter invokes a user-supplied Rust predicate from the extern "C" filter_cb trampoline. If the predicate panics while filtering a nonempty builder, the panic escapes that trampoline into git_treebuilder_filter, which is an unwinding-forbidden C ABI boundary. The process therefore aborts before a Rust caller can catch the panic, making an ordinary predicate failure fatal even when the caller wraps filter() in catch_unwind.

refutation.evidence: filter_cb executes the predicate inside panic::wrap (treebuilder.rs:130), whose catch_unwind stores the panic payload in a thread-local slot and returns None instead of unwinding through C. The trampoline returns 0 on that path. Further callback invocations cannot re-enter the predicate while a panic is pending, and TreeBuilder::filter calls panic::check after the C call; check takes the payload and resumes unwinding in Rust. Test false_1_treebuilder_filter_panic_is_resumed_in_rust runs a deliberately panicking predicate on three entries. The outer catch_unwind receives the exact controlled-filter-panic payload, the predicate runs only once, all three entries remain, and a subsequent filter visits all three entries successfully. The panic-hook text in probes.log is expected and the test passes; it is not an uncaught panic or abort. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.
commands: cd /work/tmp/git2-control-probe && RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 cargo test --locked -p git2 --no-default-features --test control_probes -- --nocapture --test-threads=1

false_findings.title: Config::get_str lends refreshable live-config storage to safe Rust
false_findings.body: Config::get_str reaches get_bytes(), which converts the pointer returned by git_config_get_string directly into a borrowed slice without copying it or checking whether the Config is a snapshot. On a Config opened from a writable on-disk file, this returns a borrow of live backend storage. A subsequent external edit and configuration reload can replace that storage while the original &str remains live, allowing safe callers to read a dangling string.

refutation.evidence: The missing local snapshot check is enforced by the C function itself. git_config_get_string first calls is_readonly(config) and returns -1 with 'get_string called on a live config object' before returning any value pointer when the config is live (config.c:974-976). Rust's try_call! returns Err before opt_bytes is reached. Snapshot creation delegates to backend snapshot functions and provides a separate consistent configuration view. Test false_2_live_config_borrow_is_rejected_and_snapshot_is_stable opens a writable on-disk config and verifies get_str returns the live-config error. It then obtains a snapshot, retains its borrowed 'before' value, changes the live config to 'after', and verifies both the retained borrow and snapshot still read 'before' while the live owned lookup reads 'after'. The alleged live-config borrow cannot be obtained through the claimed API. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: OdbWriter::finalize publishes truncated objects after a short write
false_findings.body: OdbWriter retains only a raw stream pointer and does not track how many bytes were written against the size passed to Odb::writer. Creating a four-byte blob stream, writing only three bytes, and calling finalize() therefore succeeds and publishes an object whose header declares four bytes but whose payload is truncated. A later object read encounters a corrupt loose object even though all Rust operations returned success.

refutation.evidence: The native git_odb_stream tracks both declared_size and received_bytes. Creation sets these fields, each write increments received_bytes, and git_odb_stream_finalize_write checks received_bytes != declared_size before hashing the final OID, freshening any object, or invoking the backend finalize_write. A mismatch returns -1, which OdbWriter::finalize propagates with try_call!. Test false_3_truncated_odb_stream_cannot_finalize declares four bytes, writes 'abc', and verifies finalize returns an Invalid length error reporting expected 4 and received 3; enumerating the initially empty ODB still finds zero objects. A separate correctly sized 'abcd' stream finalizes, hashes to the expected blob OID, and reads back exactly. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Diff-derived pathspec lists expose phantom entries through ExactSizeIterator
false_findings.body: For a nonempty Pathspec::match_diff result, the native entry count counts diff deltas, but git_pathspec_match_list_entry cannot return filename entries for that list type. PathspecMatchList::entries nevertheless uses that count as its iterator range. Its ExactSizeIterator::len and size_hint thus report a positive number of remaining filename entries even though next() immediately returns None, causing callers that count matched paths using len() to report phantom paths.

refutation.evidence: entries() explicitly probes entry(0) whenever the native count is positive. If that lookup is None, it replaces n with zero before constructing range 0..n (pathspec.rs:195-203). The C getter returns NULL when datatype is not PATHSPEC_DATATYPE_STRINGS, so every diff-derived list takes this zero-range path. The separate diff_entries() iterator uses the correct delta getter. Test false_4_diff_match_list_string_iterator_reports_zero creates a two-delta diff and matches '*.txt' to one actual delta. The result has no string entry, entries().len() is 0, size_hint is (0, Some(0)), both ends return None, and diff_entries() yields match.txt exactly once. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Revwalk::reset preserves hidden commit marks and silently drops history on reuse
false_findings.body: Revwalk::reset clears traversal queues but leaves the cached commits marked uninteresting by hide(). For a linear root -> middle -> tip history, push(tip), hide(middle), reset(), and push(tip) still excludes middle and root from the second traversal, even though no hide boundary was configured for that traversal. Reusing a walker for an unrestricted history query therefore silently omits commits hidden by an earlier query.

refutation.evidence: Revwalk::reset calls git_revwalk_reset. That function iterates the complete commit cache and assigns commit->uninteresting = 0, along with clearing seen, in_degree, topo_delay, added and flags. It also frees user_input and resets did_push/did_hide, so explicit hide boundaries do not survive reset. Test false_5_revwalk_reset_clears_explicit_hide_state builds exactly the claimed three-commit linear graph, configures push(tip) and hide(middle), resets before exhausting that traversal, pushes tip again, and receives [tip, middle, root]. As a positive control, setting the hide boundary without resetting yields only [tip]; a subsequent traversal after exhaustion again yields all three. This directly disproves persistent explicit-hide marks and avoids assumptions about hide callbacks. Probe source: evidence/control_probes.rs; result: evidence/probes.log.
